params.caption.prompt: Southern blues rock with a rolling mid tempo swagger, opening with a clean chiming descending guitar figure on a bright single coil bridge pickup through a spring reverb tank with no drums, doubled an octave up by a second clean guitar, then the full trio entering together, foreground electric guitar through a rocking wah pedal and a germanium fuzz into a cranked hundred watt stack with natural power tube breakup and controlled feedback, heavy finger vibrato, wide whole step bends, percussive sixteenth note rhythm scratching behind the beat, verses rolling on a single dominant seventh chord with a country rock lilt, choruses lifting on a five six one movement with a borrowed flat seventh, warm round bass playing melodic countermelody instead of roots, loose powerful live drums with a deep tuned floor tom and a fat backbeat snare, crisp shimmering cymbal decay with open airy top end on the ride and hi hat, tambourine, warm plainspoken male baritone lead vocal, slightly nasal, drawling and conversational with detailed consonants, close miked with short slap echo, shouted double tracked chorus, extended guitar jam outro with feedback and a slow fade, weary and tender and unhurried, A Mixolydian with blues thirds, vintage analog tape production with real room bleed and a clear detailed top end, A Mixolydian with blues thirds.
params.caption.lyrics:
[Intro - clean chiming guitar figure, no drums]

[Intro - full trio enters]

[Verse 1 - rolling, one chord groove]
She comes in when I'm going out
Two minutes standing in the drive
Her hands still cold off the register
Mine already stained with dye

[Verse 2 - rolling]
We keep the notes up on the door
Milk, the light bill, and be good
Twelve years of her handwriting
I'd know it anywhere I stood

[Chorus - heavy, wah and fuzz]
TWO SETS OF KEYS AND ONE FRONT DOOR
Same bed, never the same time
She gets the daylight, I get the dark
And we call that doing fine
TWO SETS OF KEYS AND ONE FRONT DOOR
Knob worn down to the brass
Nobody writes it in a song
But it holds, and it lasts

[Verse 3 - rolling]
Her mother asks are we happy
Like it's a thing you sit and choose
I say the mortgage is current
And the truck's got decent shoes

[Guitar Solo - wah and fuzz, building]

[Bridge - half time, heavy]
Sunday is the one we share
Both too wore out to talk
So we sit out on the tailgate
And we watch the weather walk

[Chorus - heavy, full band]
TWO SETS OF KEYS AND ONE FRONT DOOR
Same bed, never the same time
She gets the daylight, I get the dark
And we call that doing fine

[Chorus - heavy, doubled and shouted]
TWO SETS OF KEYS AND ONE FRONT DOOR
Knob worn down to the brass
Nobody writes it in a song
But it holds, and it lasts

[Outro - extended guitar jam, feedback, slow fade]
params.file.name: Two Sets of Keys
